g.text: (a) OUT OF DOMAIN: the drawn witness
IS: corner frame (wall x=0, floor y=0); red dashed = the corner box (0,1)^2; C = the floater (h_u=0.963 off the wall, h_v=0.848, tilt 31.7 deg);
T_u = C dropped onto the wall (blue dashed); stipple = the STRIP T_u minus C; X = the wall toucher above C (tilt 12.8 deg, lowest point y=1.84).
geometry check: X,C disjoint True; X meets T_u (area 0.094); C meets the box: NO.
Q (red) = a flat free square: gaps to C 0.084, to X 0.515, depth in T_u 0.47 -- it enters the strip. But C MISSES the corner box, so this is NOT a JAM corner: out of domain.
IS: corner frame (wall x=0, floor y=0); red dashed = the corner box (0,1)^2; C = the floater (h_u=0.525 off the wall, h_v=0.038, tilt 10.6 deg);
T_u = C dropped onto the wall (blue dashed); stipple = the STRIP T_u minus C; X = the wall toucher above C (tilt 27.7 deg, lowest point y=1.04).
geometry check: X,C disjoint True; X meets T_u (area 0.008); C meets the box: YES (area 0.359).

CLAIM (STRIP_2, open for tilted C): no unit square disjoint from C and X, inside the quadrant, has an interior point in the stipple. Tested true at 60/60 sampled domain points; proved only for flat C.
